children: CFO Eimear Bonner said higher energy prices likely will stick around until shipping flows resume through the Strait of Hormuz at a predictable level and more refining capacity comes back online,

"Until we see changes in both of those levers, prices are likely to stay elevated," while the company stays focused on putting as much supply into the market as it can and running its refineries reliably, Bonner told a WSJ Leadership Institute dinner in New York.
On Venezuela, Bonner said the country will not provide a significant source of increased supply in the short term, even as Chevron's
agreement to invest $7B to double its production there and the company has already raised output this year from the country by 15%.

, which is currently reaping the benefits of higher oil prices and deleveraging its balance sheet, is also planning for the inevitable day when prices tumble again: "Plan for volatility. Plan for uncertainty. Plan for things that can happen," Bonner said.

"We actually look at the business through the lens of multiple scenarios and multiple prices," which leads to "a very rigorous planning ritual that we do where we not only test ranges on economic growth, but we also test ranges on prices for all commodities," the CFO said.

title: Chevron CFO sees little relief anytime soon from elevated oil prices
